ARCHITECTURAL PSYCHOLOGY OFSTRESS 3
Abstract
Stress, bythe definition setforth byCohenet al.,is inherently environmental,yet,
somehow,ina world wherewecontrolmany majoraspects ofour environment, stress is
becomingan increasingly prevalentand severeconcern.Themodernenvironment, unnaturally
textureless,dull, and lifeless isnotonly unstimulating,butlacksthebiophilic connectionto
nature thathasbeenshowntorelieve psychological andphysiological stress.
In this study,weexamine therelationship betweenbiophilic environmentsandstress
through deliberatestress induction andstress reductionexercises withafocusonalternative
biophilic materials(bamboo, texturedconcrete). Inthis study,biophilicenvironmentswere found
to significantly decreasephysiological stressresponses while mindfulnessmeditationwas found
to significantly increasemoodanddecreasesomatic distress.Theresults ofthis study
demonstrate thatfurther considerationshould beinvestedinto notonlyhow, andoutof what, our
environmentsareformed but also intothe anticipatedexperienceofoccupants.

this evolutionarycontext.However, westillretainthe sameneuralmechanismsof ourancestors.
In our modernenvironment, ourancient cognitionpatternscan reactin someunexpected ways,

our connection withour material environment, likea pungentodor,or anyother persistent

ARCHITECTURAL PSYCHOLOGY OFSTRESS 8
Background
Whiletherelationship between humansand theenvironment hasbeen thesubject
of artfor centuries,scientificinquiry of environmentalpsychology onlybeganin the1960sand
70s following thedestruction ofWorld WarII and theresulting constructionboom.Early focuses
of thefield includedcrowding,childhood spaces,institutionalenvironmentsand environmental
stress (Gieseking,2014). However, after aswell ofinterestinthe 1970s,the fieldlargelydeflated
and becamean umbrellaterm for manysubfields, includinghuman factorpsychology.
In 1984,Ulrichmadethe groundbreaking discoverythat natureviews fromhospitalbeds
reduced patientpainand sped uprecovery,becomingthe father ofevidence-based design(EBD),
thearchitectural paralleltoenvironmentalpsychology. Afterhis discovery,interestinbacking
design withscienceblossomed, aswell asfascination withthespecificdesign styleof biophilia.
Biophilic designfocusesonconnectinghumans tonature throughbuilding andinterior design.
WhileStephenKellertavidly pushedfor the initialexploration after Ulrich’sfindings and
generated muchof theoriginal enthusiasm intheresearch area, itwas William“Bill” Browning
who establishedthe14patternsof biophilicdesign in2014.
Within Browning’spatterns, aretheprinciplesof usingbiomorphic formandpattern and
theincorporation of natural materials(Browning, 2014).However,the bodyofscientific
evidence backingthesetwopatterns isnot extensive,as biophilicdesign isarelatively newfield.
Therefore,this studyispredominantly putforthin aneffort toburgeontheseparticular patterns’
evidential basis.
Status Quo and Gaps
Theexisting bodyof evidencesupportingthe useof naturalmaterials indesign hasbeen
largely focusedonwood. Many differentaspects ofwood havebeen studied,including tone

texture material eventhough woodis notalways themost sustainablenor availablematerial.
Whilealternativematerialshaven’tbeen studied,intheseexperimentsfinished concreteis most
oftenthecontrol condition, meaningthat whilethey arefocusedonstudying wood,they arealso

Throughout thewood materialstudies,there isoftenanemphasis onthestudy ofstress,

measured beforeandafterentering thewood environment. Whileambientstress isrelevant, and
reflective of fieldconditions, itmay notentirely capturethe interactionbetween anenvironment
and stressshouldactive stress eventsoccurwithinaspace,leavinga significantgapinthe

Overall, therehasbeen enoughresearchonwood asa materialthat wecanproject some
preliminary conclusions,the samecannotbe saidfor biomorphic formandpattern. Whilewe
understand,fundamentally, thatbiomorphic formandpatterns have beenutilized indesign for as
far backaswehaveartifacts, therehavebeen noempiricalstudiesthat isolate biomorphicform

form ina two-dimensionalspace,withparticipants viewingnatural fractalpatterns andone
virtual reality studythatincorporated asinglenatureanalogueform, alongwithotherbiophilic
elements, howevernone specifically studiedstress.Thus,this study willbethe first toisolateand
evaluatebiomorphic form’s impactonstress.

ARCHITECTURAL PSYCHOLOGY OFSTRESS 10
Significance
This studyhassignificance inbothintellectual andrealworld implications.It
supplements existingevidenceas wellas breaksground inthesustainability andbiomorphic
form fields.Broadlyspeaking,this study isintendedtoemphasize the importanceofwhat
materialsmake upour environment, andhow theyareformed, ratherthan simply thespatial
organization or whatiscontainedwithin them.
Intellectual Merit
Themain significanceis its intellectualmerit. Thisstudyis intendedtoprovidemore
documentation for theexisting relativelysmallbodyof evidencethat supportsenvironmental
applicationsof biophilic materiality andtexture.Theinteraction betweenstress and
environmental materialityis alsoexplored throughthis study,potentially providing evidencethat
environmentscansupport orhinderstress reduction.Through thisaid orhindrance, this study
couldimply thatsome environmentalmaterials worsenoccupantstress.
Broader Implications
Through thisresearch,wehope toprovideexecutable conclusionsfor design
professionals toreduce stressfor occupants.If the hypothesisis correct,thisstudy mayprovide
supportfor bambooasa beautifulandbeneficial finishmaterialwithsimilar aestheticand
stress-reducingproperties towood. Hopefully, thisevidence mayprovideamodicumof support
for thepush toopen largebamboo manufacturingplantsin theUnited States,whichwould
greatlyincreasethesustainability ofusing bambooproducts.

Design Review
Asbiophilic designhas becomeamorepopular design style,severalstudies evaluating
cognitive andphysiologicalimpacts ofbiophilic environmentshavebeen initiatedand have
found generally positiveresults(suchas, Yin etal., 2018;Castro etal., 2022;Choe etal., 2020,
to namea few).Yinetal.documenteddecreases inphysiological stressand negativeemotions,
aswellasincreases inshort-term memoryandpositive emotions(2018). Castro etal. foundthat
biophilic environmentsdecreaseconsumer anxietyandmoderate affectiveresponses (2022).
Choe etal.discoveredthatengaging inmindfulnessin apark ratherthan aplain indoor
environment decreasedstress andrumination whileincreasingreflection and
nature-connectedness (2020). However,inorderfor thesestudies tomaintainhigh ecological
validity,theyoftenhavemultiple biophilicfactorspresentwithin theexperimentsuch aswooden
floors and windowswithdaylightanda view(aswasthe caseinYin etal., 2018).
In order tomorethoroughly understand howthe variance ofaparticular design element
impactsus, it issometimes beneficialtoisolate that factorto studyit withoutpotentially
confoundingvariables.Eveninan experimentwithjust windowswithaviewwehave
confoundingvariables.We wouldn’tnecessarily knowwhetherit wasthe vieworthe daylight
through thewindow,or an interactionbetween thetwo,that iscausingour results. Therefore,in
order totry tomake causal conclusionsandrecommendations for real-worldapplications,it may
be necessarytoisolatefactorstomeasure theirdirect impact.When selectinga factor,interms of
easeof studyand likelihood ofimpact,it maybe simplestto selectonethat is relativelystable
and occupantshavea lot ofcontact with.
Thefactor of thebuilt environmentthat wehave themost exposuretois theinterior
finish material,suchaswoodpaneling.It does notshiftthroughout the day,itis infrequently
